:::{#sol-span-subspace-practice}

Yes.
For every $a, b \in \reals$,

$$
\sbmat{a + b \\ a - b \\ 2a} = a \sbmat{1 \\ 1 \\ 2} + b \sbmat{1 \\ -1 \\ 0},
$$

so $\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{\tp{(1, 1, 2)}, \tp{(1, -1, 0)}}$.
By @thm-span-subspace,
$\mathcal{S}$ is a [subspace](#def-subspace) of $\reals^3$.

:::
